title: Fable 5.2 + Blender MCP just surprised the hell out of me
author: ralf425
selftext: I asked it to create a sick animation to a 3D Mewtwo model that could look like it's straight from the anime, and it came up with this.

comments.author: Initial_Plastic_8069
comments.body: howm any tokens ?

replies.author: ralf425
replies.body: \~110K. Felt like 5 minutes work

comments.author: 328amdev
comments.body: This is pretty nice. So Fable worked on the vfx and nothing else or did you also use it to generate the Mewtwo model itself?

replies.author: ralf425
replies.body: It just did the VFX and the movement. Imo the movements need to show off a little more energy, but the fact it got this result without any mistakes is insane to me after having tried stuff like this for the past months without any impressive results

replies.author: 328amdev
replies.body: You planning on creating a fan game?

replies.author: ralf425
replies.body: Yep I’ve been busy just messing around and trying a lot of things in the Pokémon IP! Currently focused on a fan game in HGSS style, but experimenting with 3D vs 2D. Results like this really put me in a dilemma to either make battles fully 3D, or just use it for cutscenes

comments.author: webdev-dreamer
comments.body: Every damn time I go through my 5 stages of grief and accept that there's still some value left in pursuing traditional game dev/Art, another damn impressive model lands that ruins my motivation :(

replies.author: bitterjay
replies.body: If seeing an AI tool do something you aren't capable of doing yourself demotivates you, what is the motivation for the persuit in the first place? To gain a skill? To make something you saw in your mind come to life? Or to eventually turn it into profit?

replies.author: Adventurous_Grape279
replies.body:
Probably turn a profit.

Most people in life need at least one thing that turns a profit.

replies.author: ralf425
replies.body:
I feel you as a software dev. I think you should just try to be as flexible as possible, try to learn and work with these new tools, and expand your own skillset. It opens up a lot of things you couldn’t do before.  
Creativity will still be your strongest asset.

replies.author: JorgitoEstrella
replies.body: The focus would shift to higher abstraction roles like game directing and game design

replies.author: Psychological-Arm859
replies.body: To be honest bro, think about it, if you’re a good artist and can animate vs someone that can’t, you will always produce superior works then them. You will be better than a non animator with AI. Leverage the tools and expand your imagination.

comments.author: getloadoutai
comments.body: 110k tokens for that is kinda nuts ngl. for the facing-wrong-way thing after the throw, id just describe it like a director would, "hold on mewtwo for 10 frames after release, ease the turn back to camera", way better than "fix the rotation". and imo cutscenes only for now, full 3d battles is a huge scope jump for a fan game. also keep it lowkey, nintendo lawyers are faster than any model 😅

replies.author: ralf425
replies.body:
Yep, I'm already trying to come up with my own IP to get rid of Game Freak limitations!   
And just like you say it, this was a one-shot. A round of feedback prompts would make the camera a lot more pleasing I'd say.  
Here it is a few prompts later: [https://streamable.com/k3ejmq](https://streamable.com/k3ejmq)

comments.author: SmartCustard9944
comments.body: One suggestion to make it even better. Have a video generation model create the animation, then have your AI agent use that to model the keyframes of the 3d model animation. It’s a bit like rotoscoping in classical animation.

replies.author: ralf425
replies.body: Gonna try that! For my latest version thats up in the last edit on this post I did let it use frames from the anime itself, but it might need better isolation of Mewtwo

replies.author: vampari
replies.body: What tools can we use for generate videos?

replies.author: GerJohannes
replies.body: Videos are expensive and Llms can't watch videos; they just take Frames out of it. If you do not want to spend a lot, just generate some Keyframe-Images of your wished animation and let the Model fill the in-between.

replies.author: SmartCustard9944
replies.body: Minimax H3 can be used locally

comments.author: Impressive_Ad_5917
comments.body: Sorry for my ignorance. So is this a blender scene and if so did it also create the textures/ materials and FX?

replies.author: ralf425
replies.body: No worries! Its in blender indeed, the textures of Mewtwo came with the model, but the cel shading, VFX / materials and animations were done by fable 5.2

replies.author: Impressive_Ad_5917
replies.body: Awesome!   Did you have to provide an image or something to stay on style?

replies.author: ralf425
replies.body: Nope! But in the prompts after it I did ask it to look at some of the anime’s frames

But this really may convince me to give it a shot. How was the usage for you to make this? As in, did you notice this took a significant amount of usage credit to do compared to opus?

comments.author: getloadoutai
comments.body: own IP is the move, game freak can keep their lawyers 😂 one thing id do before going deep on animation is lock the character design first, like a quick turnaround or a few reference renders, otherwise every new prompt drifts the silhouette a little. and save the feedback prompts that fixed the camera in a notes file so you can reuse them on the next clip instead of re-explaining every time. whats the IP gonna be, still monster battler vibes or something totally different?
